findings.location: Section 3 — increment_visit delivery contract / Section 6 — dead-letter recovery
findings.message: Dead-letter recovery (iteration-2 CHAO-002) closes the exactly-once loop via 'operator action' replay through the idempotent increment path, but the recovery time of that reconciliation tail is unbounded. The countstaleness window bounds WHEN an event is routed to dead-letter (and alerted), not WHEN a dead-lettered or out-of-window-skew event is reconciled — that step waits on an operator with no MTTR/RTO. RTO <= 30 min is scoped to store-loss recovery, not the dead-letter replay tail. A backlog of dead-lettered count events can therefore stay unreconciled indefinitely while still meeting every stated bound.
findings.recommendation: State a recovery-time bound (or explicit SLO/escalation target) for dead-letter reconciliation — e.g. dead-lettered events must be replayed within a named operator-response window, with the dead-letter counter feeding an SLA-bounded alert. Make the manual-reconciliation MTTR testable at TDD-01 alongside the RTO <= 30 min store-loss probe.

findings.location: Section 3 — Delivery channel (Visit-Counter-owned durable queue) / Section 6 — Read/create design-load
findings.message: Iteration-2 CHAO-001 characterizes read-pool and write-pool saturation well (design load, safe-overload margin, beyond-margin fast-fail/shed). The durable async dispatch queue that carries increment_visit off the redirect path has no characterized beyond-margin behavior of its own: when the reconciler sustainably lags the producer, queue depth grows on durable storage with no stated bound or shed/backpressure policy. The off-path design correctly protects redirects, and the queue is owned by the Visit Counter — but SPEC-01 binds the at-least-once contract to that transport, so its saturation policy is in-scope to reference. Unbounded durable-queue growth under sustained count load is the un-addressed tail.
findings.recommendation: Reference the queue's beyond-margin policy: bound the durable backlog (max depth / age) and state what happens at that bound (shed-with-alert vs. block producer vs. age-out to dead-letter), tying it to the existing reconciliation-lag metric. If the policy lives entirely in the Visit Counter component spec, cite that owner explicitly so the backpressure contract is traceable rather than absent.
